blocks.c: I want to be clear that nothing happened to Mrs. Dalisay on Hendry Street.
Nothing happened because Wen took the phone out of my hand and said four words into it, and they were not dramatic words, and they saved everything.
"Write down where you are, the time, and that you are not entering the premises. Then sign it and photograph it. Right now, in the car, on anything. Then don't move."
We heard the glovebox open. We heard a pen.

We heard, very faintly, a woman of sixty-one who had not spoken to her first supervisor in twenty-two years saying, in a wobbling voice, "You look after yourself down there, do you hear me," and then the sound of a phone camera.
Not silent. Quiet, the way the building had gone quiet at me all week, the polite quiet of something that has hit a clause it dislikes.
"Ms. Dalisay is not present," said the clerk, eventually, and it sounded, for the first time, like a machine reading a result it had not wanted. "The hearing is adjourned."
A pause of exactly the length a man takes when he is about to say something he has been told to say.
"The renewal proceeds at dawn," said the clerk. "With or without a hearing. The hearing determines the boxes. The renewal determines the caretaker."
"That," she said, "is the first time in thirty-one years it has told me something I didn't already know."
